test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 12 Nov, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Who became the Nawab of Bengal after the death of Alivardi Khan in the year 1756?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Siraj-Ud-Daulah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Siraj-Ud-Daulah became the Nawab of Bengal in 1756 after the death of Alivardi Khan, his maternal grandfather.
 
• He was the last independent Nawab of Bengal before the British East India Company gained control over Bengal.
 
• His tenure was marked by conflicts with the British, particularly the Battle of Plassey in 1757, which led to his downfall.
 
• Siraj-Ud-Daulah strongly opposed the expansionist policies of the British East India Company, particularly their fortification of Calcutta (Kolkata).
 
• The infamous "Black Hole of Calcutta" incident occurred during his tenure, which was used as a pretext by the British to launch military campaigns against him.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alivardi Khan:**

 
 
• He was the Nawab of Bengal from 1740 to 1756 and is known for his administrative and military skills.
 
• Alivardi Khan faced frequent invasions by the Marathas during his reign but managed to maintain Bengal's sovereignty.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Plassey (1757):**
 
 
• A decisive battle fought between Siraj-Ud-Daulah and the British East India Company, led by Robert Clive.
 
• The British victory marked the beginning of their control over Bengal and eventually most of India.
 
• The betrayal by Mir Jafar, a commander in Siraj's army, was a key factor in the British victory.
 
 
 
• **Black Hole of Calcutta (1756):**
 
 
• Refers to an incident where a number of British prisoners allegedly died due to overcrowding in a small dungeon in Fort William, Calcutta.
 
• This event was used by the British as propaganda to justify their aggressive policies in Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Nawab of Bengal:**
 
 
• The position of Nawab of Bengal was a highly influential role in the Mughal Empire, overseeing Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
 
• After the decline of the Mughal Empire, the Nawabs gained autonomy but faced challenges from European colonial powers.
